title: Ten Martini for the kagome lattice
credit: Extends Avila–Jitomirskaya (Ten Martini, Annals 2009) and Becker–Han–Jitomirskaya–Zworski (honeycomb, arXiv:1803.00988).
results: Found during review (Nov 2026): the general version fails. Replace each vertical edge of Z^2 by a rhombus (i,j)–(i±w,j+1/2)–(i,j+1) with w=1/(2√2) and take B=π/w: each rhombus carries flux π, α=√2 is irrational, and Aharonov–Bohm caging decouples the rows, giving σ(H_B)={0}∪±[√5−1,√5+1], which contains intervals. The problem is therefore restricted to the kagome lattice, a natural case where this caging cannot occur.
premise_risks: arXiv:2609.15812 (2026 preprint): 1D Robust Ten Martini; cited as a possible tool only, M does not depend on it.
arXiv:2611.10767 (2026 preprint): cited; M does not depend on it.
plain: A tight-binding electron hops on the kagome lattice (corner-sharing triangles) in a uniform magnetic field. Is the energy spectrum a Cantor set whenever the flux per unit cell is irrational? This is known for the square lattice (Ten Martini), the honeycomb lattice and the Lieb lattice, each by a reduction to a one-dimensional operator. Isolated eigenvalues (flat bands) are set aside by taking the derived set. The analogous claim for every periodic planar network is false: in a square lattice whose vertical bonds are replaced by π-flux rhombi, Aharonov–Bohm caging gives spectral intervals.
math: Let K be the kagome lattice with unit edge length: vertices L + {(0,0),(1,0),(1/2,√3/2)}, L = ℤ(2,0)+ℤ(1,√3), edges = pairs at distance 1. For a constant field B with vector potential A let (H_Bψ)(x) = Σ_{y∼x} e^{i∫_{[x,y]}A} ψ(y) on ℓ²(V(K)), and 2πα = B·covol(L) = 2√3 B. Let Σ' be the derived set of σ(H_B). Prove or disprove: for every irrational α, Σ' is a Cantor set (nonempty, compact, perfect, nowhere dense). (The analogous statement for all periodic planar graphs is false: Aharonov–Bohm caging in a square lattice whose vertical edges are replaced by π-flux rhombi gives spectral intervals at irrational α.)
